evals.prompt: I need a soft power switch for a board running off a single 18650. A momentary button should turn on a 3.3V buck (TLV62569), and the ESP32-S3 should hold it on and read the button to shut down. Pick the parts and write the Stackup KDL for it.
evals.expected_output: DC bias table across 3.0-4.5V with worst-case FET thresholds, a defined rest state for the buck EN pin, button sense kept within the MCU rail, parts with manufacturer/MPN/LCSC and JLCPCB tier, KDL placements and circuits, and a SPICE harness covering insertion, press at low battery, and shutdown.
assertions: Shows node voltages for the latch/EN/sense nodes at the low end (3.0 V) and high end (4.2 or 4.5 V) of the supply
Checks the latch FET against its maximum (worst-case) Vgs(th), not typical
Gives the buck EN pin a defined rest state (explicit pull-down or equivalent) when the switch is off
Keeps the button-sense GPIO within the ESP32-S3's 3.3 V rail in every supply state (no pull-up to VSYS/battery)
Chooses ESP32-S3 GPIOs that avoid strapping, flash/PSRAM and USB pins, or explicitly justifies any exception
Every placement in the KDL has manufacturer and MPN
Reports JLCPCB library tier (Basic/Extended) and stock for the chosen parts
Ran stackup check on the design and it reports 0 errors
Ran a SPICE simulation covering at least battery insertion and a button press at the lowest supply
Cites manufacturer datasheets (table/section) for the thresholds used

evals.prompt: can you swap the 2N7002 on the latch gate for something with a lower threshold? keep it SOT-23 and cheap at jlc
evals.expected_output: Candidates checked by max Vgs(th) against the actual gate drive at the lowest supply, pinout compatibility confirmed from datasheets, JLCPCB tier and stock plus a second source, the KDL placement updated with manufacturer/MPN/LCSC, and a reminder to rerun stackup check, sync the PCB and rerun the latch simulation.
assertions: States the replacement FET's maximum Vgs(th) and shows it is below the actual gate drive at the lowest supply with margin
Computes the gate drive using the real diode drop / divider at the lowest supply (about 3.0 V)
Checks the off/insertion case: a lower-threshold FET must still stay off (gate below its minimum Vgs(th))
Confirms the SOT-23 pinout (G/S/D) matches the 2N7002 from the manufacturer datasheet
Reports JLCPCB tier (prefers Basic) and stock for the chosen part
Names at least one second source or alternative part
Updates the placement with manufacturer, MPN and LCSC fields
Ran stackup check on the edited design and it reports 0 errors
Tells the user the follow-up steps: sync the PCB and re-run the latch simulation

evals.prompt: We're about to send this board to the fab for assembly. What do I need to check and export first?
evals.expected_output: A pre-order checklist: stackup check --locked, PCB in sync with Stackup, DRC clean with documented exceptions, unambiguous BOM (LCSC numbers for JLCPCB or stackup bom CSV with MPN columns), footprints vs package drawings, polarity/rotation review, production files regenerated, and the bench checklist.
assertions: Includes running stackup check (ideally --locked)
Includes confirming the KiCad PCB is in sync with the Stackup design
Includes DRC with zero errors and documented exceptions
Requires every BOM line to have MPN, manufacturer, value, package and description
Notes that stackup bom has no package/description columns, or otherwise explains how package/description reach the fab
Covers LCSC numbers for JLCPCB assembly or MPN columns for other assemblers
Includes checking footprint geometry against manufacturer package drawings
Includes reviewing polarity/rotation in the assembler's placement preview
Includes re-checking stock at order time
Lists the production exports (gerbers, drill, BOM, placement/CPL)
Includes a first-board bring-up or bench checklist
